title: Condo Mortgage Requirements in SC: The 2026 Rule Changes
description: Fannie Mae ended Limited Review for condos in August 2026. What a building must pass now: repairs, reserves, rentals, condotels, and what to do if it fails.
h1: Did the 2026 Condo Loan Changes Make Your Building Harder to Finance?

faq.a: A non-warrantable condo is a unit in a building that does not meet Fannie Mae's building rules, so a conventional loan on it cannot be sold to Fannie Mae. Common reasons are hotel-style operations, unfunded critical repairs, one owner holding too many units, or too much commercial space. You can still finance it with a portfolio or non-QM loan.

faq.q: Did Fannie Mae get rid of Limited Review for condos?
faq.a: Yes. Fannie Mae retired Limited Review for loan applications dated on or after August 3, 2026. Units in established buildings of more than 10 units now need a Full Review, FHA project approval, or a Fannie Mae review.

faq.q: Can I get a conventional loan on a condo I plan to rent out?
faq.a: Yes, if the building passes the review. Renting your own unit is allowed. The building fails if it requires a rental pool, shares rental profits with the HOA, or runs hotel services such as a front desk or daily cleaning.

faq.q: Does a special assessment stop a condo loan?
faq.a: Not always. Your lender reviews each special assessment. If it pays for a critical repair that is not yet fixed, the building is ineligible. A special assessment for routine work does not stop the loan by itself.

faq.q: How much must a condo HOA keep in reserves?
faq.a: Under Fannie Mae's Full Review, the HOA budget must put at least 10% toward replacement reserves. A professional reserve study showing the building is adequately funded can be used instead.

faq.q: Do small condo buildings need a review?
faq.a: Usually not. Fannie Mae waives the building review, apart from a few basic requirements, for detached condos, buildings of two to ten units, and attached units in five- to ten-unit buildings that are not part of a larger development.
